headline: 72-6262. Same; certification of completion required, alternatives; duties of school boards.
source: Kansas Office of Revisor of Statutes
blurb: This Kansas law, which dates to 1961, requires pupils entering a Kansas school for the first time to show proof of the tests and shots the state health secretary requires, or to give a doctor's statement or a parent's statement of religious objection instead.

headline: Measles among Members of a Drum and Bugle Corps -- Arkansas, California, Kansas
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: A 17-year-old from England who joined a drum and bugle corps in Hutchinson, Kansas, developed a measles rash on June 19, 1983, and five cases were reported among the 150 corps members during a tour of 24 states.

headline: Current Trends Pertussis Surveillance -- United States, 1986-1988
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: A 1986 whooping cough outbreak in Kansas accounted for 1,030 cases, which CDC called the largest outbreak reported in the United States in the previous 10 years.

headline: Assessment of Undervaccinated Children Following a Mass Vaccination Campaign -- Kansas, 1993
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: Kansas vaccinated 7,120 children on April 24 and 25, 1993, in the first weekend of Operation Immunize, a campaign started after a state survey found 52% of children entering school had been fully vaccinated by age 2.

headline: Rubella Among Hispanic Adults --- Kansas, 1998, and Nebraska, 1999
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: Kansas received reports of 35 confirmed rubella cases from April 22 to July 14, 1998, and 28 of them were in workers at meat-packing plants in one region.

headline: Hepatitis A and Meningococcal vaccines to be required for 2019-20 school year
blurb: Kansas health officials approved rules adding hepatitis A and meningococcal vaccines to the shots required for school, with two doses of hepatitis A vaccine needed for kindergarten and first grade in the 2019-20 school year.

headline: Kansas Department of Health and Environment Announces End of Measles Outbreak in Southwest Kansas
source: Kansas Department of Health and Environment
blurb: Kansas health officials declared the southwest Kansas measles outbreak over on August 21, 2025, after 87 confirmed cases since January, more than 90% of them in people who were not vaccinated.
